bands.summary: Sanaa falls, the blockade tightens, a war that reshapes Yemen - and reaches the Red Sea.

bands.label: Marginalization and insurgency: the Saada wars
bands.summary: The Houthi movement emerges, the state depletes itself fighting it, a conflict that sets the stage.

bands.label: Empires, unification attempts, and failed consolidation
bands.summary: Two Yemens, one Britain, the fracture that independence could not mend.

bands.label: The strait before empires recognized it
bands.summary: Incense routes, sultanates, Ottomans and Portuguese - and the geography that made disruption possible.

frames.label: Nov 2023
frames.note: The story begins with the first Houthi seizures and missile strikes on shipping in November 2023. The attacks read as a Gaza spillover - direct response to the Israel-Hamas war. This is the frame most Western media and regional security analysts open with.

frames.label: 2014 civil war
frames.note: The story begins with the Houthi takeover of Sanaa and the Saudi-led intervention that followed. The Red Sea attacks read as one front of a decade-long conflict - the same Houthis now striking shipping. Common among Yemen specialists and regional geopolitical analysts.

frames.label: Saada wars
frames.note: The story begins with six Saada wars between 2004 and 2010. The Houthis read as a movement forged by two decades of insurgency and marginalisation. Invoked when the argument turns to Yemen's internal fractures.

frames.label: Two Yemens
frames.note: The story begins with the two Yemens - British Aden and the imamate north, then rival republics - and the 1990 unification that never fully consolidated. The attacks read as one symptom of a state that never finished nation-building. Common in academic and humanitarian framings of Yemen.

frames.label: Ancient strait
frames.note: The story begins in antiquity - Bab al-Mandab as a strategic chokepoint for millennia: incense routes, Ottoman-Portuguese rivalry, the Suez opening in 1869, British Aden as a coaling station. A local actor's ability to disrupt global shipping reads as geography made manifest. Invoked when discussing why this narrow strait matters to the world.
